questions.question: When comparing two Naive Bayes classes for the same document, which score is sufficient for choosing the larger posterior?
options: The document length alone
The prior of the other class without any word counts
log prior plus the sum of log likelihoods for the words
The raw word order interpreted as a decimal number
questions.explanation: The evidence term is shared by classes. Taking logs turns the product of the prior and conditional word probabilities into a sum.

questions.question: With vocabulary size 3, spam has 80 occurrences of free in 150 tokens and non-spam has 5 in 115. After add-one smoothing, which comparison is correct?
options: Both probabilities are exactly 0 because smoothing removes rare words
P(free|non-spam)=115/5 is the probability used by the model
The two probabilities must match because classes share a vocabulary
P(free|spam)=81/153 is much larger than P(free|non-spam)=6/118
questions.explanation: Laplace smoothing adds one to the count and vocabulary size to the denominator. The observed word remains much more associated with spam.

questions.question: What simplifying assumption gives Multinomial Naive Bayes its name?
options: Features are conditionally independent given the class
All classes have exactly the same prior
Every document contains one word
The model learns a nonlinear decision boundary
questions.explanation: The model factorizes the class-conditional likelihood into per-feature terms. The independence assumption is often false but can still rank classes effectively.

questions.question: Which variant matches each feature type?
options: Gaussian for word counts, Bernoulli for temperatures, Multinomial for one binary flag
Multinomial for word counts, Bernoulli for binary presence, Gaussian for continuous values
All three variants require continuous targets
Bernoulli is the only variant that can represent class priors
questions.explanation: The likelihood family should match the observed feature representation: counts, binary indicators, or continuous measurements.

questions.question: A test document contains a word absent from the training vocabulary. What does Laplace smoothing help with?
options: It changes the word into a labeled training example
It proves the word is evidence for every class equally
It keeps an unseen word from forcing a class probability to zero
It removes the class prior from the posterior
questions.explanation: Add-one smoothing assigns a small nonzero likelihood to an unseen count, preventing the whole product from collapsing to zero.

questions.question: Why can Naive Bayes be a useful baseline for sparse text even when its independence assumption is unrealistic?
options: It models every word interaction exactly
It never needs labeled documents
It is guaranteed to outperform logistic regression
Fast likelihood estimates can produce strong class rankings in high dimensions
questions.explanation: The assumption is a bias, but the resulting model is cheap and often effective for sparse counts. Its accuracy still needs empirical comparison.
